notes:
1. In the SQL editor's criteria section, clearing a criterion now removes the condition it had added to the SQL, instead of leaving a stale filter such as "xxx = '0'" behind.
2. The FabLIMS LSN, Lot Genealogy and Package Info queries now return rows in a stable, meaningful order — LSN by manufacture date, and the genealogy and package queries by work order lot and date.
3. New Script template: Lamination Genealogy — queries FabLIMS lot genealogy and LSN for the work order lots you list, and builds a self-contained ECharts dashboard showing the raw face/film/backer usage feeding each work order's packaged lots, with hover details.

1. The SQL editor and the query Builder now keep separate result grids — running a Builder query no longer overwrites the SQL editor's results, and vice versa.
2. Running the Process_Data template now shows a step-by-step progress panel (the SQL query, then the Python wide-table conversion), so you can see it is still working instead of appearing frozen.
3. In the SQL editor's criteria section, date fields now show only the date (no time), and the Yield Summary template's criteria were updated to match the current SQL.

1. Query results now have a search box at the top: type to filter rows across every column at once, with a one-click clear button.
2. In the SQL Builder the table/view selector gained its own search box, so you can find a table or view by name instead of scrolling through a long list.
3. The Analyze tab's Copilot prompt now tells the AI to deliver its findings as a self-contained HTML report with Apache ECharts charts, save it to your Downloads folder and open it when done, and — when the task needs your input — show a native Windows dialog the same way this app does (console/tkinter prompts cannot work in a non-interactive run).

1. Fixed the failed update that could leave the app showing an error page (HTTP 500) after restarting: the app now starts correctly on the newly installed version, and an update can no longer install into a leftover backup folder.

1. Large SQL editor queries (200,000+ rows) now stream in batches, so results start appearing immediately and no longer stall or fail partway through.
2. Excel/CSV export from the SQL editor no longer stops at 100,000 rows — the full result is exported.
3. Databricks connections now remember your authorization, so the sign-in window only appears when a fresh sign-in is actually needed (instead of on every test or page refresh), and the leftover callback tab closes itself.
